edges.description: The mutant receptor autophosphorylates without angiopoietin ligand.
Constitutive TIE2 signalling activates the downstream PI3K-AKT axis.
AKT signalling suppresses endothelial cell death and sustains the lesion.
An AKT/FOXO1 axis reduces PDGFB and with it pericyte recruitment.
edges.target: PDGFB Downregulation and Mural Cell Deficiency

edges.description: Endothelial cells that do not die accumulate into expanding channels.
Without adequate mural cell support the vessel wall cannot resist dilatation.
edges.source: PDGFB Downregulation and Mural Cell Deficiency

edges.description: Venous stasis inside the malformation consumes clotting factors locally.
Thin-walled bowel lesions bleed into the gut lumen.
Used to test pharmacological suppression of the pathway node, reading out lesion regression.
edges.limitations: A xenograft of human cells in mouse rather than a genetic mosaic model, so it reproduces the lesion but not the post-zygotic mosaic origin.

nodes.description: Clinical endpoint. The bowel malformations bleed slowly and repeatedly rather than catastrophically, producing occult loss, melena and progressive iron-deficiency anaemia. This is the dominant source of morbidity and the endpoint against which treatment is judged, since haemoglobin and transfusion requirement are the practical outcome measures.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and Safety of Sirolimus for Blue Rubber Bleb Nevus Syndrome: A Prospective Study.
evidence.snippet: The characteristic gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding from multiple VM lesions causes severe chronic anemia which renders most patients depend on lifelong blood transfusion and frequent endoscopic treatment with dismayed outcomes.

nodes.description: The convergent structural lesion: dilated, thin-walled venous channels lined by endothelium and poorly invested with smooth muscle. These are the malformations seen in skin and bowel, and they enlarge over time rather than involuting.

evidence.reference_title: AKT/FOXO1 axis links cross-talking of endothelial cell and pericyte in TIE2-mutated venous malformations.
evidence.snippet: characterized by dilated and immature veins with scarce smooth muscle cells (SMCs) coverage

nodes.description: Endoscopic sclerotherapy, band ligation and snare resection of accessible gastrointestinal lesions. Together with transfusion this is what most patients depend on before disease-directed systemic therapy, and it targets the bleeding lesions directly rather than the pathway.

nodes.description: Mutant endothelial cells resist apoptosis and show increased survival, invasion and colony formation. The lesion therefore persists and expands rather than remodelling.

evidence.reference_title: Blue Rubber Bleb Nevus (BRBN) Syndrome Is Caused by Somatic TEK (TIE2) Mutations.
evidence.snippet: both cause ligand-independent activation of TIE2, and increase survival, invasion, and colony formation when expressed in human umbilical vein endothelial cells

nodes.description: A murine xenograft of TIE2-mutant endothelial cells that forms venous malformation-like lesions and permits therapeutic testing. Combination ponatinib and rapamycin caused lesion regression in this model.

evidence.reference_title: Ponatinib Combined With Rapamycin Causes Regression of Murine Venous Malformation.
evidence.snippet: Combination treatment with the ABL kinase inhibitor ponatinib and rapamycin caused VM regression in a xenograft model based on injection of HUVEC-TIE2-L914F.

nodes.description: The mutant TIE2 receptor signals constitutively rather than in response to angiopoietin. In endothelial cells this increases survival, invasion and colony formation, the cellular phenotypes that underlie lesion growth.

evidence.reference_title: Blue Rubber Bleb Nevus (BRBN) Syndrome Is Caused by Somatic TEK (TIE2) Mutations.
evidence.snippet: both cause ligand-independent activation of TIE2, and increase survival, invasion, and colony formation when expressed in human umbilical vein endothelial cells

nodes.description: Venous stasis within the ectatic channels consumes clotting factors locally, producing a chronic consumptive coagulopathy with elevated D-dimer and sometimes low fibrinogen. It is the eighth and final step of the causal chain, the disease's most specific laboratory marker, and the reason these patients carry both thrombotic and perioperative bleeding risk.

evidence.reference_title: Elevated D-dimer level in the differential diagnosis of venous malformations.
evidence.snippet: Elevated D-dimer level is highly specific for VMs (pure, combined, or syndromic)

nodes.description: AKT-dependent regulation of FOXO1 reduces endothelial PDGFB expression. Because PDGFB is the signal by which endothelium recruits pericytes and smooth muscle, mutant vessels are covered by fewer mural cells, which is the structural reason the channels are floppy and prone to dilate.
nodes.id: PDGFB Downregulation and Mural Cell Deficiency

evidence.reference_title: AKT/FOXO1 axis links cross-talking of endothelial cell and pericyte in TIE2-mutated venous malformations.
evidence.snippet: VMs with TIE2-L914F mutation showed lower expression of PDGFB and α-SMA than normal veins.

nodes.description: Constitutive TIE2 signalling drives the PI3K-AKT-mTOR axis. This is the branch point of the disease: it both suppresses endothelial apoptosis and, through AKT-dependent regulation of FOXO1, reduces PDGFB expression. It is also the node that sirolimus acts on, which is why mTOR inhibition is effective across lesion types.

evidence.snippet: Dominant-negative Akt inhibited the pro-survival activity of mutant Tie2

nodes.description: A post-zygotic somatic mutation of TEK arises in an endothelial-lineage cell. Multifocal disease, including BRBNS, is characteristically driven by double mutations in cis - two somatic changes on the same allele - which distinguishes it from the single somatic alleles typical of unifocal sporadic venous malformation.

nodes.description: Segmental or wedge resection of bowel carrying a high burden of focal lesions, and emergency surgery for intussusception, volvulus or obstruction. Reserved for disease that is focal enough to resect.

nodes.description: First-line systemic therapy for diffuse or unresectable disease. Sirolimus inhibits mTOR, the node downstream of the constitutively active TIE2-PI3K-AKT axis. In a prospective study of BRBNS it reduced lesion size and raised haemoglobin, with only grade 1-2 adverse effects.
